items.title: 67250_John Collins oral history interview
items.q: I heard him play it and he played it so beautifully I said I'm going to do that tune.

ctx.x: A new style. Well, before then it was Louie Armstrong, but Roy came along with a tremendous technique and strong lip, you know. He could play high, higher than anyone else, you know. And he was just -- he was an innovator. After Roy came Dizzy. Dizzy went in another direction. There was also another great trumpet -- there were so many great trumpet players during that era. There was Charlie Shaver. I think one of the all time great trumpet players.

always loved his playing, and I on -- when I appear I always -- if I'm going to do a concert I always include one tune, "My Man." I love that tune and everybody identified it with Billie Holiday. I identify it with Charlie Shavers, When I play that tune -- that's why I play it. I heard him play it and he played it so beautifully I said I'm going to do that tune. And I always think of Charlie whenever I play this tune. Because he was a beautiful trumpet player, and he made a record of "My Man" that is just sheer…

So during that time you had some great trumpet players, and of course Roy at that time was considered the president, as I stated before. Paul Whiteman was writing for (or something) the Saturday Evening Post Company, used to have this jazz poll. And he gave Roy the title of the king of the trumpet players, the world's greatest trumpet player. So on the strength of that we came back to New York from Chicago, and played at the Savoy, opposite as I -- I know I'm repeating myself but opposite Erskine Hawkins and the…
